p.x:
Demain by Hermann Hesse
The world is an egg; we are the sparrow-hawk within; we must break the shell so the world will be reborn. We who would deign to break the egg wear the mark of Cain on our brows. I worship Abraxas, who is God and the Devil at once. No one hears of Abraxas by chance. We make new gods and fight them; we find old gods and fight them too, even as we worship, for they too must die. 
Growing up is hard. It’s hard, and no one understands, but some authors try. Hesse may very well have succeeded. I found Siddartha at 20, and I find Demain at 23, as a Christmas gift from my dear friend @arithmoquine. A book as a gift is a wonderful thing — it is about as close as you can get to giving someone a little spyglass that shows them a piece of your heart. I’ve been giving them for years and only recently have I made friends who will actually read them, so the gravity of receiving this as a gift is not lost on me. And what a fascinating, serious, philosophical spyglass into a young man’s soul this book is. 
I would recommend this book to young person, or anyone of any age undergoing the at times painful process of breaking their shell and finding their destiny, but it is a delight to look a little closer into Henry’s heart and all the more delightful to see myself standing there.
